title: bromus arvensis var. patulus
intro: Bromus arvensis var. patulus, commonly known as wild brome, is a type of grass that belongs to the Poaceae family and is native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa. It is used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antispasmodic properties. The therapeutic actions of wild brome include reducing fever, relieving cough and respiratory issues, and treating gastrointestinal problems. The bioactive constituents of wild brome include flavonoids, saponins, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
